content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have a damper actuator with a 500-ohm input impedance for a 0-20mA signal, and I also have a [product_name] analog output module. The catalog specifies that the resistance between M and I ports should be below 250 ohms. What issues might arise if I connect my actuator to this module? I've already bought the equipment and can't replace it, so I need to use what I have. Looking forward to your advice.
You mentioned having a [product_name]. Why did you post this in the [version_no] section instead of the one for [product_name] hardware?
Apologies, I was looking at topics related to 'Analog Output Impedance' and didn't notice I was in the [version_no] area. I have started a topic at [url]. Sorry for any confusion.
Dear [user_name], Could you offer your assistance?
Thread closed as the question was posted twice. The second post with the subject 'Analog Output Impedance' can be found in the [product_name] hardware section. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user is seeking guidance on whether connecting a damper actuator with higher input impedance than recommended to an analog output module is safe or poses operational risks. They are unable to replace the hardware and want to understand possible consequences of using equipment outside of specified limits. There is some confusion regarding posting in the correct technical forum, but their main concern is about hardware compatibility and system reliability.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wishes to receive information on the risks and effects associated with connecting their actuator to the output module, with hopes for a clear answer about whether it will function correctly and safely under these conditions.
